notes.filename: Are You Your Friends- Friend- Poor Perception of Friendship Ties Limits the Ability to Promote Behavioral Change.md
notes.fulltext_access: Full 13-page primary PLOS ONE article and its main text accessible; supplementary file not independently reviewed.
verified: Dependent measure is mean daily activity in P2 divided by mean daily activity in P1, notwithstanding the article's shorthand 'change'.

Authors' labels and directions are correct: 'ego perceived friend' means alter nominates ego (incoming), and 'alter perceived friend' means ego nominates alter (outgoing). Reciprocal and incoming coefficients are positive/significant; outgoing is not significant in Table 1.
The relevant directionality regression combines Peer See and Peer Reward and omits Control; all three intervention conditions are identified in the note.

The tie-type classifiers are correctly named: logistic regression uses one feature per task, and Random Forest uses the ten identified SE/SC features; ROC AUC is reported. The note's shorter summary does not misstate these procedures.
DOI and publication date match the article.
notes.bibliography: The 68 links were preserved from the prior snapshot, but were not title-by-title reconciled against the article's 52 numbered references; several links are unresolved and some may be aliases/duplicates. No completeness caveat appears in the note.
exact_fixes: Add a bibliography provenance caveat stating that the captured 68 links have not been reconciled against the source's 52 references and do not represent a verified complete bibliography.

Use the source author form 'Alex Pentland' in the bibliographic metadata (the note currently inserts 'Sandy', which is not present in the article byline), unless that is an intentional linked-author display alias documented elsewhere.
notes.limits: Claims about classification and the intervention were checked in the article body; supplementary robustness details were not audited.

notes.filename: Bias Reduction in Social Networks Through Agent-Based Simulations.md
notes.fulltext_access: Full 10-page primary arXiv paper accessible; Springer publication metadata was not independently opened in this re-audit.
verified: The paper traces approximately 173,000 users and 1.5 million edges, then focuses the reported feed experience/outcomes on 5,599 central/core users.

Trait prevalence scenarios are P(X=1) in {0.05, 0.15, 0.50}; 36 hourly ticks, 0.083 activation probability, lognormal tweet count parameters, like probabilities 0.20/0.05, and reset at t=24 match Sections 3.1-3.3.

Random and reverse-chronological feeds, NCF, Wide & Deep, and greedy MinimizeRho are accurately described. NCF/Wide & Deep retrain each tick for 10 epochs, and MinimizeRho greedily chooses edges that minimize the rho-kx difference.
The note correctly identifies feed lengths and core-user exposure measures. Its model loop and prose distinguish the large traced network from the 5,599 users whose experience is analyzed.
Abstract and research questions are supported by the paper.
notes.bibliography: The 28 captured links include unresolved placeholders; their titles/order were preserved from the earlier snapshot, but they were not reconciled against the source bibliography. The note has no explicit completeness caveat.
exact_fixes: Add a bibliography provenance caveat stating that the captured links have not been reconciled against the paper's bibliography and completeness is unverified.
notes.limits: The model-claim audit passed. The listed publication date is identified as the Springer proceedings eBook date in the initial audit, but that metadata was not independently re-opened in this pass.
